reader.requirement: At --std 85 TERMINATE, after at least one GENERATE, must produce every control footing from minor to major (FINAL last), then the report footing. While it does, the prior control values must be available to the control-footing and report-footing SOURCE clauses and USE procedures, as for a break at the most major control. Other groups (the last page footing) see the current values, sum counters total as for a most-major break, and afterwards the control items hold their current values again.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.TerminateDiscardsSavedNextGroup: from 2002 an absolute NEXT GROUP save location is discarded at TERMINATE; at 85 it stays for the first control footing's fit test

DialectBehavior.ControlFootingPageGroupsSeePriorControlValues: at 85 the page footing TERMINATE presents (and page groups a footing's page advance reaches) see the current values; from 2002 they see the priors

reader.edition-search: Grepped ReportWriter.cs for DialectBehaviors.IsActive: lines 734, 964, 1080 and 1490. Two of them (1080, 1490) are on the TERMINATE path; ReportWriter.Edition is set from --std by the generated construction.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a page footing at TERMINATE sees the current control values (1985 SR5 forbids PH/PF from naming a control data-name anyway, and the compiler refuses that with COBOL6825), and a saved absolute NEXT GROUP survives into the control footings. The control-footing and report-footing order and prior values are the same at 85 and 2023.

reader.notes: TerminateCore saves the current values and restores the priors, runs ProcessControlFootings(0) (minor to major), presents the page footing (current values at 85), then the report footing, and restores the current values last. The probes show the order, the priors, the rolled-forward sums and the restore. DISPLAY of a sum counter shows '+03', which concerns the SUM clause, not this rule.
